_comment: Toolchain pin for the `layout/power/` flow (`klt power`) -- the IR-drop
and electromigration read issue #346 asks for. Checked, not merely
recorded: `layout/power/run_power.py` refuses to run under a `klt`
whose `klt version --format json` identity does not match the two
pinned fields below.
WHY THIS FLOW HAS ITS OWN PIN. Same argument layout/erc/toolchain.json
makes one flow along, for the same reason: layout/toolchain.json pins
`85b8125` and every committed DRC/LVS report was minted under it, and
layout/erc/toolchain.json pins `67d617f` and every committed ERC report
was minted under THAT. Re-pinning either to reach `klt power`'s two
2026-09-22 fixes would re-baseline an evidence trail that has nothing
to do with IR drop. This flow therefore carries its own, newer pin and
re-baselines only itself.
WHY THIS COMMIT SPECIFICALLY -- and why an OLDER `klt power` is not
merely less convenient but WRONG for this block. `klt power` has
existed since klayout-tools#844/#845/#846, but two defects found while
standing this flow up would each have produced a confidently wrong
number on ADC_BLOCK rather than an error:
* klayout-tools#2259 -- a via attached to the nearest node on the
whole net instead of the polygon it actually lands on. ADC_BLOCK's
supply is a Metal1 trunk with Poly2 stubs (layout/adc-top/lib/
geometry.py's channel router), which is exactly the topology that
defect fragments: the rail came apart into disconnected components
and the solve reported ~0 mV droop. Fixed by klayout-tools#2269
* klayout-tools#2260 -- no `devices[]` carve-out, so a drawn resistor
or capacitor body on a declared role was solved as wire. ADC_BLOCK
has both (the comparator's poly load resistors on Poly2, the CDAC's
MiM unit caps bridged by Via4 geometry) -- the same two bodies
layout/erc/adc_block.supply-spec.json already declares for
`klt erc` (klayout-tools#2183). Without the carve-out the IR/EM
verdict is computed on a net that is not the rail. Fixed by
klayout-tools#2271 (`bc53cd6f`).
Both fixes are in the tagged release `v0.6.0`, which is what this file
pins -- a release rather than a bare main-branch commit, so an outside
reader re-running this flow gets a build with a name, not a snapshot of
somebody's main.
klayout_package is pinned too, and unlike layout/erc/'s it is asserted
by run_power.py: `klt power`'s connectivity model IS klayout's
LayoutToNetlist, and the resistive network it builds -- which polygons
merge, where a segment's endpoint nodes land -- is that library's
output. A different klayout build is a different network, and this
flow's committed droop numbers are solved on the network, not on the
GDS. `v0.6.0` itself expects `0.30.10` (`klayout_version_expected` in
`klt version --format json`), which is also what layout/erc/ recorded.
Bumping this pin is a reviewed change, like every other pin in this
repo: re-run `python3 layout/power/run_power.py`, read the diff of the
committed reports case by case, and write what moved into the new
record under layout/power/records/. The seeded control in cases.json
exists precisely so a bump that silently stops solving fails the run
instead of being inherited as a clean verdict.
minimum_upstream_issue: klayout-tools#2269 (via-attaches-to-the-polygon-it-lands-on) and #2271 (`devices[]`); both released in v0.6.0
